subject: health
unitTitle: Mental Health, Stress, and Support Networks
title: Correction and reflection: help-seeking plans
essentialQuestion: How can understanding mental health, stress, and support networks help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: A help-seeking plan names several trusted contacts, routine and urgent routes, how to start the conversation, and what to do if the first route is unavailable.
Match the response to the level of need: use a practical coping step for ordinary strain, add trusted support when functioning is disrupted, and use urgent help for immediate danger.
For help-seeking plans, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Respond to fictional situations with boundaries, coping options, trusted support, and urgent escalation when indicated.
studentTask: Complete a fictional support-plan card for help-seeking plans: identify one observable signal, choose one immediate coping or communication step, name a routine support route and an urgent route, and explain why the plan does not make a peer responsible for care.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in help-seeking plans; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the help-seeking plans task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
